messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Polish, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Polish line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition (from Step 1) | Target Word/Phrase (Polish) | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|--------------------------------------|-----------------------------|------------------------|--------| | **ché** | causal conjunction “because” | **bo** | because | OK | | **questa** | demonstrative adjective “this” | **ta** | this | OK | | **bestia,** | noun “beast” | **bestia** | beast | OK | | **per** | preposition introducing the relative clause “for which” | **przez** | through / because of | OK | | **la** | definite article (fem. sg.) – no Polish equivalent | — | (none) | **UNNECESSARY** | | **qual** | relative pronoun “which” referring to *bestia* | **którą** | which (fem. acc.) | OK | | **tu** | pronoun “you” (subject of *gride*) | — (encoded in verb *wołasz*) | you | **UNNECESSARY** | | **gride,** | verb “cry out” | **wołasz** | you cry out | OK | | **non** | negation “not” | **nie** | not | OK | | **lascia** | verb “lets / allows” | **pozwala** | allows | OK | | **altrui** | indefinite pronoun “any other (person)” | **nikomu** | to anyone | OK | | **pasar** | infinitive “pass” | **przejść** | to pass | OK | | **per** | preposition “along / through” (governing *via*) | **drogą** | by way (instr.) | OK | | **la** | definite article (fem. sg.) – no Polish equivalent | — | (none) | **UNNECESSARY** | | **sua** | possessive adjective “its” | **jej** | its / her | OK | | **via,** | noun “way” | **drogą** | way (instrumental) | OK | | **ma** | coordinating conjunction “but” | **ale** | but | OK | | **tanto** | adverb of degree “so much / so … that” | **tak** | so | OK | | **lo** | pronoun “him” (object of *'mpedisce*) | **go** | him | OK | | **'mpedisce** | verb “hinders” | **powstrzymuje** | hinders | OK | | **che** | complementizer “that” (introducing result clause) | **że** | that | OK | | **l'uccide;** | verb phrase “kills him” | **zabija** | kills | OK |

### Items to Note - **UNNECESSARY**: - *la* (appears twice) – Italian definite article has no counterpart in Polish. - *tu* – the subject pronoun is omitted in Polish; the verb form *wołasz* already encodes the second‑person singular.
- **MISSING / WRONG / GRAMMAR**: none. All required meanings are present, and the Polish translation respects gender, number, and case agreement.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Polish script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Polish text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
